facts.claim: The Cursor harness ships as dist/cursor/ — a ready-to-copy distribution that users place into their project, matching the pattern of existing Claude, Kiro, Codex, and opencode harnesses.
facts.rationale: All AI-DLC harnesses follow the same distribution model: generated output in dist/<name>/ that users copy wholesale into their project root.
constraints: dist/ is GENERATED and never hand-edited
Must be byte-parity reproducible via bun scripts/package.ts --check
implications: CI must guard drift with --check flag
All authoring happens in harness/cursor/ and core/, never in dist/cursor/
facts.evidence_quote: The harness ships as dist/cursor/ — a ready-to-copy distribution that users place into their project

facts.claim: The harness authored surface lives at harness/cursor/ containing: manifest.ts, emit.ts, skills/aidlc/SKILL.md, onboarding.fills.ts, and hooks/aidlc-cursor-adapter.ts.
facts.rationale: Follows the established pattern where each harness has a thin authored surface that the packager consumes. The emitter handles Cursor-specific structural divergence.
constraints: Must implement HarnessManifest contract from scripts/manifest-types.ts
implications: Five primary files to implement
emit.ts is required (not optional like Claude)

facts.claim: harnessDir is '.cursor' — Cursor's native discovery paths all start with .cursor/ so rules, skills, hooks, commands, and MCP config are found without user configuration.
facts.rationale: Using .cursor as harnessDir means zero Cursor settings changes required. Same files work for IDE, cursor-agent CLI, and cloud agents.
constraints: The dist/cursor/.cursor/ directory ships in output only — does NOT exist in the aidlc-workflows repo itself
implications: All native surfaces are auto-discovered by Cursor
No user configuration needed for first use
facts.evidence_quote: Cursor's native discovery paths all start with .cursor/

facts.claim: tierFlavor is 'claude' because Cursor uses standard Anthropic model identifiers (claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-opus-4-8). Add a separate 'cursor' tierFlavor only if Cursor's model naming diverges from raw Anthropic identifiers.
facts.rationale: Cursor's primary model is Claude with standard Anthropic naming. No point in adding a new flavor that would be identical.
constraints: Model selection is user-governed (UI picker), not per-agent file config
Tier system informs orchestrator instructions about preferred model class but cannot enforce
implications: No new tier mapping code needed initially
Orchestrator can suggest model class in instructions but user makes final choice

facts.claim: rulesRename is null. Core method-knowledge (memory/) is transposed into .cursor/rules/*/RULE.md by the emitter with appropriate YAML frontmatter. Core rules/ directory stays at standard location in workspace shell.
facts.rationale: Cursor's native .cursor/rules/ directory has a specific format (RULE.md with frontmatter). The emitter transforms core content into this format rather than simple file renaming.
constraints: Each rule folder must contain RULE.md with YAML frontmatter
Best practice: under 500 lines per rule
implications: emitter handles the transformation, not the coreDirs projection
Method knowledge split into always-apply (core methodology) and agent-decided (phase-specific)

facts.claim: Agent delegation is instruction-driven, not file-driven. Cursor has no per-agent file format (.agent.md equivalent). The orchestrator skill instructs which persona to adopt, subagent delegation uses Cursor's built-in Task tool, and agent behavioral rules are loaded via .cursor/rules/ based on context.
facts.rationale: Unlike Copilot (.agent.md) or Kiro (agent JSON), Cursor manages subagents natively through its Task tool. The AI-DLC 14-agent roster works through prose instructions in the orchestrator, not native agent registration.
constraints: Cannot restrict subagent tools via file config — only via hook gates (subagentStart)
Similar to Claude Code's approach
implications: No agent/*.json or .agent.md files needed in dist/cursor/
Orchestrator SKILL.md must contain comprehensive delegation instructions
Hook gates needed for subagent safety controls

facts.claim: Hooks fail open by default. Security gates must explicitly set failClosed:true to ensure they block on hook failure.
facts.rationale: Cursor's default fail-open behavior means hooks that crash or timeout will not block the agent. This is a platform design choice for resilience, but security-critical gates need explicit opt-in.
constraints: failClosed: true required for all security-critical gates
implications: Hook adapter must set failClosed on AI-DLC state-transition guards and shell gates
Audit-only hooks can remain fail-open

facts.claim: Cloud agents do NOT fire sessionStart/sessionEnd events. Use beforeSubmitPrompt for initialization in cloud agent contexts.
facts.rationale: Cloud agent lifecycle differs from IDE — no persistent session concept. beforeSubmitPrompt fires on every prompt submission regardless of execution environment.
constraints: User-level hooks (~/.cursor/hooks.json) do not run in cloud agents either
implications: Session init hook must use beforeSubmitPrompt (not a dedicated sessionStart event)
Must detect first-prompt condition to avoid re-init on subsequent prompts

facts.claim: The packager auto-discovers harnesses by scanning harness/ for manifest.ts files. Zero edits to package.ts are needed to add a new harness.
facts.rationale: Architecture supports extensibility without touching the build tool itself. Each new harness only needs its manifest.ts to be discovered.
constraints: manifest.ts must implement HarnessManifest type contract
implications: Adding harness/cursor/manifest.ts is sufficient for packager integration — no package.ts changes

facts.claim: Only one text transform exists for .md files: {{HARNESS_DIR}} token substitution. The packager substitutes .cursor for this token.
facts.rationale: Minimalism by design — keeping transforms to a single well-known token prevents complexity in the build pipeline.
constraints: No other variable substitution in markdown files
implications: Prose in core/ references the harness directory generically; packager fills in .cursor at build time

facts.claim: Success criteria require 8 conditions: (1) packager generates complete dist/cursor/, (2) --check passes byte-parity, (3) distribution copyable to fresh project with /aidlc --doctor passing, (4) orchestrator launches via /aidlc, (5) rules provide method context, (6) hooks fire correctly, (7) all existing tests pass + new tests green, (8) works across IDE, CLI, and cloud agents.
facts.rationale: Comprehensive acceptance criteria ensuring the harness is production-ready across all execution environments.
constraints: All 8 must pass — not partial acceptance
implications: Need tests covering packaging, hook firing, doctor check, and cross-environment compatibility

facts.claim: Must not use legacy .cursorrules format. Only the new .cursor/rules/*/RULE.md folder format is allowed.
facts.rationale: Legacy formats are deprecated. Using only the modern format ensures forward compatibility and takes advantage of activation types (Always, Auto Attached, Agent Requested, Manual).
constraints: No .cursorrules file in dist/cursor/
implications: All method knowledge must use the folder-based RULE.md format with proper frontmatter

facts.claim: Development work happens on a feature/cursor branch using conventional commits with feat(cursor): prefix.
facts.rationale: Standard branching strategy for isolated feature work. Conventional commits enable automated changelogs.
constraints: MIT-0 license required for all contributed code
implications: Branch already named; commit messages must follow pattern

facts.claim: Out of scope: VS Code extension development, changes to core/ methodology/stages/agents (beyond doctor arm), custom MCP server integration, Background Agent / Cloud Agent configuration, Team Rules dashboard integration.
facts.rationale: Scope boundary keeps the work focused on the harness surface without extending into platform-specific extensions or core methodology changes.
constraints: Only core/ change permitted: --doctor arm in core/tools/aidlc-utility.ts
implications: Design must work within existing core capabilities
No new agent types or stage modifications

facts.claim: The stop hook supports followup_message for self-correction loops with loop_count guard. This maps to AI-DLC's self-correction/retry mechanism.
facts.rationale: Cursor's stop hook can trigger re-entry for self-correction, similar to how other harnesses handle retry loops.
constraints: Must include loop_limit to prevent infinite loops
implications: Hook adapter can leverage followup_message for AI-DLC's forwarding-loop enforcement

facts.claim: The proposed dist/cursor/ layout includes: .cursor/{skills/aidlc/SKILL.md, rules/aidlc-method/RULE.md, rules/aidlc-phase-*/RULE.md, hooks.json, hooks/, commands/*.md, cli.json, tools/}, aidlc/ (workspace shell), AGENTS.md, .cursor-plugin/{marketplace.json, plugin.json}.
facts.rationale: Layout follows Cursor's native discovery paths while maintaining AI-DLC's standard workspace shell (aidlc/) at project root.
constraints: dist/cursor/.cursor/ lives only in generated output — not in aidlc-workflows repo
implications: Five rule folders (1 always-apply method + 4 agent-decided phases)
Three command files (status, jump, scope)
Single hooks.json registry pointing to hook scripts

facts.claim: Cursor's built-in Task tool handles subagent delegation with types: generalPurpose, explore, shell. The orchestrator instructs delegation through prose; Cursor manages subagent lifecycle natively.
facts.rationale: Cursor has first-class subagent support via its Task tool — no need to simulate delegation through custom mechanisms.
constraints: Cannot scope subagent tools via files — only via subagentStart hook gates
implications: Orchestrator SKILL.md must instruct when to delegate and which Task type to use
subagentStart hook needed for safety controls on delegated tasks
facts.section: Mapping AI-DLC Concepts to Cursor Surfaces
